findings.title: internal/relay is one package that mixes HTTP adapters, SaaS rules and SQLite persistence
findings.principle: module_responsibilities, business_rule_ownership, dependency_direction and saas_responsibilities; the Go SaaS standard requires independent application/domain packages with external HTTP and infrastructure, and the principles require package boundaries where strict isolation is needed.
findings.impact: Quota, key, billing and tenant rules are implemented inside net/http handlers that receive *sql.Tx; changing a rule or a table forces edits in the same function and prevents narrow reuse or unit-level verification. Transaction boundaries, authorization and response mapping are coupled, so unrelated console capabilities share one package and one change surface.
findings.recommendation: Keep cmd/model-relay as assembly. Introduce packages for the rule-rich console capabilities named by the standard (for example identity, access, catalog and accounting) with application and domain packages; move SQL into infrastructure implementations of interfaces declared by those modules; restrict net/http to an httpapi adapter that calls application operations. Move methods such as Store.admit, Server.manageLimits and Server.tenantBills into the owning application operation and a persistence interface. Update architecture.json to declare and enforce those boundaries.
findings.validation: Re-run make architecture-check after adding rules that forbid httpapi -> domain/SQLite and domain -> HTTP/SQL/application. Preserve behavior with the existing console_contract_test.go, console_http_test.go and metering_regression_test.go suites. This is an import/structure recheck, not a runtime claim.

findings.title: Routing policy and runtime state depend on HTTP requests and SQLite writes
findings.principle: gateway_upstream_separation and dependency_direction; the Go model-gateway standard says routing provides selection and observation operations and owns weight/sample/cooldown state without processing HTTP responses or SQL.
findings.impact: beginAttempt both selects a route and opens/persists a SQLite transaction while accepting an *http.Request; acceptLatency writes route_latency_evidence. Routing algorithms and health/latency state cannot be exercised or changed without the HTTP layer and schema, and management/schema changes can touch selection code.
findings.recommendation: Extract routing policy and runtime state (weighted counters, cooldown, latency pools and selection observations) into a routing package whose API accepts candidate snapshots and observation events, not *http.Request or *sql.Tx. Keep orchestration in routed_proxy.go/gateway; persist route_selection_evidence and route_latency_evidence through an evidence-store interface implemented outside routing.
findings.validation: Check that the routing package imports no net/http or database/sql; preserve behavior with routing_latency_test.go, routing_http_test.go and routing_contract_regression_test.go. No runtime correctness is inferred.

findings.title: One Server object and one mutex own unrelated console, routing, health, latency and session state
findings.principle: state_ownership and module_responsibilities; unrelated capabilities should not depend on one shared mutable object, and session, request, routing, health and business state need explicit owners.
findings.impact: Console handlers, routing dispatch, upstream checks, latency evidence and success evidence all mutate fields of Server under the same broad lock. Slow management or storage work can serialize unrelated dispatch and console paths, and state lifetime/cleanup is hidden inside one struct.
findings.recommendation: Keep Server as the HTTP/composition entry point. Move routing/health/latency maps into the existing routeRuntime/routeHealth/latencyPool owners behind a routing-state interface, and give the checking registry and session/auth state their own owners and lock scopes. Avoid holding the console-wide mutex while beginning a storage transaction.
findings.validation: Recheck field ownership and lock use in server.go, routing.go, routing_latency.go and console_api.go; preserve existing routing and console tests as behavior safeguards. This remains a static concurrency-boundary review.

findings.title: workspace.js is one global feature bundle with no feature-owned UI, state or API
findings.principle: frontend_features, module_responsibilities and state_ownership; features own business UI, interaction state, business API and cleanup, shared transport stays business-neutral, and public entry points constrain dependencies.
findings.impact: All business pages share one state object, one renderPage switch and shared edit/table/detail helpers. Changes to one page can affect unrelated pages, cleanup is global, and there is no module boundary that exposes or restricts each feature's API.
findings.recommendation: Split workspace.js into ES feature modules for models, services, keys, tenants, limits, usage, billing, records and playground; each feature owns its render/action state and cleanup. Keep shared/api business-neutral and keep table, modal and formatting helpers in shared modules. The page router should import feature entry points rather than one global renderPage/monolith.
findings.validation: Recheck the static import graph and public feature entry points; preserve behavior with the existing Node/browser tests and workspace HTML/CSS asset loading. No new business rules are proposed.

findings.principle: standards_alignment; project rules and executable declarations must agree with supplied target standards and must not waive requirements merely by describing the current code.
findings.impact: The architecture check can pass because it only enforces module-level path membership; it cannot detect that rule-rich SaaS capabilities lack application/domain boundaries or that routing depends on HTTP/SQL. findings.recommendation: Update architecture.json and the backend spec to declare startup, httpapi, application/domain modules and infrastructure implementations for the rule-rich console capabilities, plus the routing/gateway split. Add enforceable import rules; keep the current honest limitation text until the packages exist, but do not treat the single relay module as satisfying the SaaS/gateway standards.
findings.validation: Re-run make architecture-check with compliant and violating import samples for the new module declaration; preserve existing behavior tests as safeguards. This is a declaration/CI gate review, not a runtime validation.
